title: Shared Decision-Making Across Languages in Healthcare
summary: Learn how healthcare teams translate decision aids, explain risk, use AI medical interpretation, and confirm patient understanding across languages.
body_markdown:
###


Use AI interpretation with clinical quality controls to run the conversation in real time: introduce the decision, explain options in short segments, pause for the patient's response, and confirm numbers and negations are preserved exactly. Pair spoken interpretation with a translated decision aid, then close with teach-back, asking the patient to explain the options and risks in their own words before you document a choice.


###


Opalite Health covers both sides of the workflow: real-time AI medical interpretation across 150+ languages and dialects for the spoken encounter, and medical document translation across 400+ languages for written aids, consent forms, and discharge instructions. Guardian applies automated and human-supported quality checks across outputs, which matters when number accuracy and negation errors can quietly change clinical meaning.


###


State the baseline chance first, then the changed chance, using the same population size and time period. For example, following NICE's framing: 1 in 1,000 people experience the outcome without the intervention; 2 in 1,000 do with it. Pair that with labeled icon arrays, confirm the interpretation preserved every number and qualifier, then ask the patient to restate the figures back to you.


###


Google Translate is a general consumer tool with no clinical quality controls, no encounter documentation, and no healthcare-specific validation. Opalite Health is built for medical communication, with dialect-aware interpretation, Guardian quality checks designed to catch negation and numeral errors, and multilingual scribing that produces a structured clinical note from the encounter.


###


Verify the source text is in plain language first, then check that medication names, negations, probabilities, time frames, and option balance survived translation without change. Confirm labels match graphics and test the aid with intended readers, since back-translation alone cannot confirm patient understanding. Release the aid only after validated automated controls or qualified review confirm accuracy, applying closer review to consent forms and discharge instructions.
